title: SBI Sees India at 7.2% Growth to Close FY26
excerpt: State Bank of India projects Q4 FY26 real GDP at 7.2% and FY27 at 6.6%, as domestic demand holds firm against global headwinds.
body:
India's State Bank of India released its latest Ecowrap research report on May 11, projecting real GDP growth of 7.2% for the January–March quarter of FY26 — a figure that would cap a strong fiscal year even as the global economy wobbles. The full-year growth for FY26 is likely to settle at 7.5%, even as the outlook for the following year remains subject to geopolitical shifts.

**What the numbers show:**
High-frequency data showed a minor decline in the fourth quarter, yet overall economic activity remained resilient. Strength in rural consumption, supported by both farm and non-farm sectors, continues to provide a solid foundation for growth. Urban consumption also maintained a steady upward trajectory since the previous festive season, bolstered by fiscal stimulus. Credit growth has accelerated to 16.1% in FY26, up from 11% in FY25 — a sign that money is moving through the real economy.

**Why FY27 will be tougher:**
The report expects the growth trajectory to moderate slightly, with real GDP growth of 6.6% for FY27, primarily due to the ongoing economic implications of global geopolitical disturbances. The IMF recently lowered its world growth forecast to 3.1% for 2026, citing supply chain disruptions caused by conflicts in the Middle East. However, contrary to the global trend, the IMF slightly increased India's growth projection to 6.5% for 2026-27, driven by strong domestic demand. SBI notes its FY27 estimate will be revised as new data arrives. The report also flagged that the rupee needs structural changes on the Balance of Payments front, including streamlining import substitution and export competitiveness.

**What to watch:**
The National Statistics Office is scheduled to release provisional estimates of annual GDP for FY2025-26 along with GDP estimates for the January–March quarter on May 29, 2026 — that official print will either confirm or complicate SBI's call.
